description: 'Starts, continues, or logs project work: finds or creates the work item, works out where it stands, and runs its next step through to a built result. # Work on

Voice: write to the owner in plain English. Claude Code: follow the project's Plain English output style. Codex: follow the "How to write replies" section of `AGENTS.md`.
Shared rules: the work plugin's `references/conventions.md` (saving, section edits, history, branches) and `references/trackers.md`, two folders above this skill's folder (`../../references/`). To open another skill, Claude Code uses the Skill tool; Codex reads that skill's `SKILL.md`. Run each `toolkit` command alone, on its own line: in Codex a command joined by `&&`, `;`, a pipe, or a heredoc, or run from a script, runs inside the sandbox and fails. Give text with `--text`, or a file in a new `mktemp -d` folder (never a fixed `/tmp` name, deleted right after the command). Never change a record with a script.

## Steps

1. No session briefing in this conversation: run the command below. Exit code 4 (no `.toolkit.json`): open `project-setup` and stop. When the briefing or a `toolkit work` command lists changes found in the tracker (a moved or renamed folder, a new parent, a missing item), tell the owner each one in one line before other work.
   `toolkit brief`
2. Find the item: the id the owner named, or a title in the list that matches the request. Two possible matches: ask one question naming both. No match: it is new. When `PROJECT-ROADMAP.md` names the item, read its phase there too.
   `toolkit work show <id>`
   `toolkit work list`
3. Size a new request. Setup is not a work item: never create one for setup steps; owner steps go in the reply and in the current focus under "Waiting on the owner". "New work", "track", "work item", or "done properly" always makes an item, and content the owner has not described is a question for him, never a quick edit. A quick edit (one sitting, no choice for the owner, no behavior recorded in `requirements/`, nothing bound for production): do it and report it, with no item. "Later", "backlog", "park that": check the list for a duplicate, create the item, write the owner's words unchanged into Starting request, reply "Logged as WI-014 (bug, backlog). Not started." and stop. Anything else: create it the same way, titled in the owner's words (say the title in one line), and continue.
   `toolkit work new --title "<title>" --type <type> --stage 01-discovery`
   `toolkit work edit <id> --section "Starting request" --text "<the owner's words>"`
4. A substantial goal whose item shows `delivery: not-offered`: open `work-delegate` first. When it asks the offer, wait for his answer before building. Quick questions and small edits get no offer.
5. Route by where the item stands, using the item and the "Continue with" column of the lifecycle. Requirements not approved and type `build` or `data-load`, or the owner answered the questions that set them, or asked for it done properly: `work-requirements`, which shows them to him for approval. More than one reasonable way to build it and no approved design: `solution-design`. A `build` item going to planning without a design: say so in the final reply, not a progress line ("One way to build this: <approach>. I'll build it that way; say 'design first' to stop me."), and put the reason in a history note. An item that changes committed files goes through stage 07 (its own worktree), never onto the default branch. Too big for one build: `work-organize`. Stages 09 to 11: `work-check`. Stages 12 to 14: `work-finish`. `waiting_on: owner`: ask that one question first (`work-decide`) and keep working on anything it does not block. Say the route in one line ("WI-012 is waiting for your OK on the requirements; opening work-requirements."). Never ask the owner which stage it is in.
   `toolkit work lifecycle`
6. Plan (stage 06): Roadmap phases `P1`, `P2` and tasks `P1-T01` (Work, Deliverable, Done when, Depends on) from the design's "Build and verification plan", in the table and checkbox format in this skill's own `references/planning.md` (the `references/` folder beside this `SKILL.md`; read it first).    `toolkit work edit <id> --section Roadmap --set-file <file>`
   `toolkit work edit <id> --section Tasks --set-file <file>`
7. Build (stage 08) on the item's own branch and worktree, never on the default branch. In Codex, `git worktree add`, `git add`, and `git commit` need the owner's approval and escalated permissions (`sandbox_permissions` set to `require_escalated`, with a one-line reason), because the sandbox keeps `.git/` read-only: say in one line what each does before Codex asks. Refused without asking: show him the exact command, ask him to approve it or run it in a terminal, and set the item waiting on the owner. Salesforce: `sf-component-tracker` on each metadata change; production data only through `sf-data-change`.
   `toolkit work set <id> --stage 08-build`
8. When the owner is needed: add an Open Questions row (next free `Q-` number) with "owner" as who decides, set the item waiting on the owner, keep working on tasks that do not depend on the answer, and tell him in one line.    `toolkit work edit <id> --section "Open Questions" --append-row "| <next Q-id> | <question> | <affects> | Open | owner |"`

9. Last task done: open `work-check`. This skill never records approvals, Done, merges, or deploys.

## Agents

- `builder`: one per independent build task, only when `work-delegate` recorded a team or the owner agreed to one. The main agent merges each builder's branch into the item's branch, then ticks the task.
- `researcher`: one per unknown found while planning or building.
- `acceptance-checker`: a plan check after step 6, before the build, when the plan has several builders, parallel tasks, or a shared environment. Paste in the requirements, the design's "Build and verification plan", the Roadmap, and the Tasks, and ask for a plan check.
- How to brief them: `../../references/helpers.md`.
- Codex: this plugin's agents do not load there. Read the agent's file in this plugin's `agents/` folder and give its full text, with the brief, to a native Codex worker: the `spawn_agent` tool, started without this conversation (`fork_turns` set to `none`), so a checker never shares the builder's thread. With no worker, do the work yourself and say that no independent check ran.

## Sizing a request

- **Quick edit, no item:** one sitting, no decision for the owner, and it does not change behavior recorded in `requirements/`. Examples: fix a typo, rename a variable, answer a question. Report what changed in one line.
- **Log only:** the owner says "later", "backlog", "park that", "not now", or "log a bug". Create the item at `01-discovery`, fill Starting request with his exact words, and stop. Do not start the work.
- **Work item:** everything else. A request that grows past a quick edit while you work on it becomes an item then, with the owner's words as the Starting request.
- Types: pick the closest from the lifecycle's type list. `build` and `data-load` need approved requirements before stage 03 is passed; the CLI refuses otherwise. A change to what the product does, to Salesforce metadata (`force-app/`), or to anything bound for production is `build` (data changes are `data-load`), never `task`, even when it looks small.

## Routing notes

- The lifecycle's "Continue with" column is the default. The item's real state decides: for example, a `task` type item with no open choices can skip requirements approval and go straight to planning, with the reason in a history note.
- Stages may be skipped, repeated, or revisited. Record a short reason when a move is not obvious.
- A worktree whose branch names an item (`claude/wi-<number>-<slug>`) belongs to that item. The briefing says so. Work on that item there.
- Several items at once: recommend what can proceed independently, what depends on another outcome, and which decision would unblock the most work. See this skill's own `references/planning.md`.
- `PROJECT-ROADMAP.md` holds the project's phases (`P01`) and deliverable-sized work units, each naming its work item ID; item detail stays in the tracker. A new item that is one of those units gets its ID written into the unit, saved with `publish-docs`. An item's own phases (`P1`) are a different thing and live in its Roadmap section.

## Never

- Never record an approval, Done, or a cancel here. Those belong to `work-requirements`, `solution-design`, `work-check`, `work-decide`, and `work-finish`.
- Never merge, deploy, or write production data.
- Never create a second tracker or a local copy of items kept in Notion, GitHub, or Jira.

# WI-001: Add a Tier picklist field to Account — solution design

**Requirements:** WI-001, R-01, approved by Mike on 2026-09-27  
**Design status:** Approved  
**Requirements checked:** WI-001 requirements, 2026-09-27  
**Last updated:** 2026-09-27  
**Design approval:** Approved by Mike on 2026-09-27

## What this design solves

The sales team needs to rank Accounts with an optional Tier field. Gold, Silver, and Bronze must appear in that order, with Gold highest and no default. Every Account viewer must be able to read Tier. Only Sales Manager profile users and system administrators may edit it. Tier must appear directly below Rating on Account Layout and have a description and help text. This design covers the field, access, layout, and verification. It does not change existing Account data.

## Requirements and design readiness

The approved requirement is ready for design. The independent requirements analyst found no material gap on 2026-09-27. The sandbox's full Account layout and access configuration still need a read-only inventory before implementation.

| Requirement | Status in work item | Design coverage | Remaining decision or gap |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| R-01 — Account ranking | Finalized, Mike, 2026-09-27 | Options A and B; Option B has a stated condition | No requirements decision. Verify org configuration before build. |

## What exists today

The repository declares `force-app` and source API 62.0 in `sfdx-project.json`, but `force-app` does not exist yet. A read-only sandbox check on 2026-09-27 confirmed `tkv2-sbx` is connected at API 62.0 and a Tooling API query returned `Account Layout`. A query for `Account.Tier__c` returned no CustomField record, but the current field and full layout metadata were not retrieved. Rating's exact position, assigned Lightning pages, Dynamic Forms, profiles, and effective field access remain unverified. The build must inspect the org before creating or replacing any component.

## Constraints and assumptions

| Type | Constraint or assumption | Source and status | Effect on the design |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Constraint | Use Salesforce built-in features and show two options. | Mike, 2026-09-27, confirmed | Both options use standard field, layout, and access controls. |
| Constraint | Do not deploy profile metadata from source. | Project permissions-source-control rule, confirmed | Profile field access needs recorded Setup steps and verification. |
| Constraint | Agents never deploy to or change production. Sandbox deployment needs Mike's approval. | AGENTS.md and Salesforce org safety rule, confirmed | Production release is an owner handoff. |
| Assumption | `Account Layout` governs the relevant record detail view. | Not verified | Inventory all assignments and Dynamic Forms before build; stop for scope correction if placement cannot be met. |

## Design options

### Option A — Profile field permissions

#### Approach

Inspect sandbox `Account.Tier__c` first. If it exists, reuse or adjust it; otherwise create the optional picklist. Use Salesforce field-level security to grant read access to every Account viewer and edit access only to the Sales Manager and System Administrator profiles. Configure profile permissions in Setup. Do not deploy profile XML. Put Tier directly below Rating on `Account Layout` and verify the actual assigned view for every affected Account viewer. If existing layout or Dynamic Forms assignments prevent that placement within the approved scope, stop for a scope correction.

This uses the approved built-in approach. The requirements describe a complete result for the named field, access rule, and layout. The build still needs an inventory of the sandbox field, actual profiles, permission sets, permission set groups, every affected Account layout and Lightning page assignment, Dynamic Forms, and `Account Layout` metadata before making changes.

#### End-to-end behavior

An Account viewer opens an Account record and sees Tier directly below Rating in the actual assigned view. Tier may be blank on existing and new Accounts. The viewer can read the selected value and help text. A user with the Sales Manager or System Administrator profile can select Gold, Silver, or Bronze, save, and clear the field when the user also has Account and record edit access. Other Account viewers can read but cannot edit through the record interface or API. Check every affected layout and page assignment, including Dynamic Forms.

#### Requirement coverage

| Requirement | Build or reuse | Why it meets the requirement | How to check it |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| R-01 — Account ranking | New or changed `Account.Tier__c` picklist with Gold, Silver, Bronze in that order; no default and not required. New or changed description and help text. Changed assigned Account views as needed within approved scope. Reused profile field-level security, configured in Setup. Audit all field grants. | The field stores the ranking and allows blank values. Gold is highest. Field-level security grants read to all Account viewers and restricts edit to the two approved profiles when no other grant adds edit. Every affected assigned view must show Tier directly below Rating. | Inspect field metadata. Inventory every affected layout, Lightning page, and Dynamic Forms assignment and confirm placement in each actual view. Build an effective-access matrix for every affected profile and permission-set or group combination, including multiple grants; verify read and edit for each combination. Save all three values and blank as Sales Manager and System Administrator users. Confirm denied record-interface and API edits for every non-manager combination. |

#### Technical shape

**Components and files**

- New or changed after sandbox inspection: `Account.Tier__c` custom field metadata in `force-app`, using the existing `sfdx-project.json` API version 62.0. Set label `Tier`, type Picklist, active values Gold, Silver, Bronze in that order, no default, and `required=false`.
- New field description: `Ranks an Account as Gold, Silver, or Bronze for sales prioritization. Gold is highest.`
- New field help text: `Select Gold, Silver, or Bronze to rank this Account. Gold is highest. Leave blank if the Account has not been ranked.`
- Changed: `Account Layout` metadata, with Tier immediately below Rating in the same layout column. Retrieve the full layout first; preserve its other fields and sections. Inventory every affected Account layout and Lightning page assignment, including Dynamic Forms. If other assigned views need changes, confirm approved scope before editing them.
- Reused: Salesforce profile field-level security, configured in Setup for the profiles found by the access inventory. No profile XML is included in the deploy package.
- New: work-item package manifest containing only the field and approved view metadata changes. New manual access configuration and verification steps in the work item's deployment instructions.

**Data and state**

- `Tier__c` is an optional single-select value on each Account. The ordered values are Gold, Silver, Bronze. Gold is highest. No automation fills blank values. Existing Accounts remain blank until a permitted user sets a value.
- Do not migrate or alter existing Account records.

**Access and security**

- Inventory profiles of all users who can view Account, including users whose Account access comes from a permission set. Give each such profile read access to `Account.Tier__c` in Setup. Give field edit access only on the Sales Manager and System Administrator profiles.

Salesforce permissions can add together; a read-only profile setting does not cancel an edit grant from a permission set.
- Verify the real profile names and assignments before configuration. Enumerate every distinct effective profile, permission-set, and permission-set-group combination among Account viewers, including users with multiple grants. Verify effective field read and edit for each combination. Do not assume layout visibility enforces editing rights.

**Integrations**

- No integration or automation is requested. Existing API clients can read the field only if their Salesforce user has Account and field read access. An update needs Account and field edit access.

**Operations**

- Deploy only the field and layout metadata through the work-item package to the sandbox. Configure profile field permissions in Setup after the field exists. Record the exact profile settings and permission-set audit as manual release steps for the owner; agents do not deploy to or change production.
- If a new profile or permission set later grants Account access, an administrator must check `Tier__c` read access and ensure edit remains restricted. Profile Setup changes are not captured by this package.

#### Tradeoffs and risks

| Tradeoff or risk | Effect and response |
| --- | --- |
| Profile field permissions are manual and absent from source control. | The release needs recorded Setup steps and access verification in each target org. Recheck after profile or permission changes. |
| Permission sets and permission set groups grant permissions cumulatively. | An edit grant outside the Sales Manager or System Administrator profiles would break R-01. Audit grants before and after configuration, then test a non-manager Account viewer. |
| The exact position of Rating in `Account Layout` is not yet verified. | Retrieve the layout and place Tier immediately after Rating in the same column. Review the metadata diff and rendered record so other layout content is preserved. |
| Account viewers may have different layout assignments or Dynamic Forms pages. | Inventory every affected assignment and verify Tier directly below Rating in each actual view. If approved scope cannot achieve this, stop for a scope correction. |
| The repository has no `force-app` source today; sandbox field existence is unresolved. | Inspect the sandbox first. Reuse or adjust `Tier__c` if present, or add it if absent. Keep the package narrow. |

#### Build order

1. Inspect sandbox `Account.Tier__c` existence; inventory Account-viewing profiles, effective permission combinations, every affected Account layout and Lightning page assignment, Dynamic Forms, and `Account Layout` metadata. Depends on sandbox read access. Complete when field status, the access matrix, view assignments, and Rating's exact position are recorded. Stop for scope correction if approved changes cannot give every affected viewer the required placement.
2. Add or adjust `Account.Tier__c` custom field metadata with the approved values, order, optional setting, no default, description, and help text. Depends on step 1. Complete when metadata review shows every setting without a duplicate field.
3. Add Tier directly below Rating on `Account Layout` and each other approved assigned view that needs it; create a narrow work-item package manifest. Depends on steps 1 and 2. Complete when diffs preserve unrelated content and every affected view can show the required placement.
4. Validate and deploy the narrow package to the sandbox using the sandbox alias from `.toolkit.json`. Depends on step 3. Complete when Salesforce accepts the metadata and the field appears on the intended layout. Do not target production.
5. Configure profile field permissions in sandbox Setup: read for all Account-viewing profiles, edit only for Sales Manager and System Administrator. Audit permission sets and groups for unwanted edit grants. Depends on step 4. Complete when the access matrix matches the approved rule.
6. Test saving Gold, Silver, Bronze, and blank as Sales Manager and System Administrator. Verify effective read and edit for every affected profile and permission-set or group combination, including denied API edits for each non-manager combination. Check Tier below Rating in every actual assigned Account view. Depends on step 5. Complete when R-01 is observed for the full affected set.
7. Prepare the owner's production release instructions with the narrow package, manual profile settings, permission-set audit, and verification steps. Depends on step 6. Complete when the owner has reviewable commands and steps. Production deployment and configuration are owner actions.

### Option B — Dedicated edit permission set

#### Approach

Inspect sandbox `Account.Tier__c` first. Reuse or adjust it if present; otherwise create the optional picklist. Give all Account viewers field read access. Give field edit access through a new `Account_Tier_Edit` permission set assigned only to active users with the Sales Manager profile. Keep field edit access on the System Administrator profile. Put Tier directly below Rating in every affected assigned Account view. Use Salesforce Setup to manage profile field permissions; do not deploy profile XML.

The requirements describe a complete result for the field, access rule, and layout. Before building, inventory the sandbox field, Account-viewing profiles, effective permission combinations, Sales Manager users, every affected layout and Lightning page assignment, Dynamic Forms, and `Account Layout`. If approved view changes cannot show Tier below Rating to every affected viewer, stop for scope correction. Manual permission-set assignments cannot guarantee the strict profile-tied rule between a profile change and the assignment update. Option B is conditional and inferior to Option A unless a dependable assignment mechanism is available and verified in the target org. Salesforce documents User Access Policies as a possible built-in mechanism for granting and removing permission sets on user create or update using profile criteria, but target-org availability and the exact grant and removal behavior are unverified. Do not select Option B on an assumed automation.

#### End-to-end behavior

An Account viewer opens an Account record and reads Tier directly below Rating in the actual assigned view. Tier can be blank. An active Sales Manager profile user who has Account edit and record access receives `Account_Tier_Edit` and can select Gold, Silver, or Bronze, save, or clear the value. A System Administrator with Account edit access can do the same through profile field edit access. Other Account viewers can read Tier but cannot edit it through the record interface or an API update. Every affected assigned layout and Dynamic Forms page must show the placement. A profile change requires an assignment change; manual processing leaves a period in which access may be wrong. Do not claim R-01 is met until the target org's assignment mechanism and profile transitions have been tested.

#### Technical shape

**Components and files**

- New or changed after sandbox inspection: `Account.Tier__c` custom field metadata in `force-app`, using the existing `sfdx-project.json` API version 62.0. Set label `Tier`, type Picklist, active values Gold, Silver, Bronze in that order, no default, and `required=false`.

- New field help text: `Select Gold, Silver, or Bronze to rank this Account. Gold is highest. Leave blank if the Account has not been ranked.`
- New: `Account_Tier_Edit` permission set metadata with `Account.Tier__c` field read and edit permissions. It grants no Account object or record access by itself.
- Changed: `Account Layout` metadata, with Tier immediately below Rating in the same layout column. Retrieve the full layout and preserve its other fields and sections. Inventory every affected Account layout and Lightning page assignment, including Dynamic Forms. Confirm approved scope before changing other assigned views.

- New: work-item package manifest containing only the field, permission set, and approved view metadata changes. New manual profile configuration, assignment, audit, and verification steps in the work item's deployment instructions. A User Access Policy is a possible conditional addition only after target-org capability and behavior are verified.

**Data and state**

- `Tier__c` is an optional single-select value on each Account. The ordered values are Gold, Silver, Bronze. Gold is highest. No automation fills blank values. Existing Accounts remain blank until a permitted user sets a value.
- Permission-set assignments are org data. The package installs `Account_Tier_Edit` but does not assign it to users. Manual assignments may diverge from profile membership after a user update.

**Access and security**

- Inventory profiles of all users who can view Account, including users whose Account access comes from a permission set. Give each such profile read access to `Account.Tier__c` in Setup. Keep field edit off those profiles except System Administrator.
- Set `Account.Tier__c` read and edit permissions on `Account_Tier_Edit`. Assign it only to active users whose current profile is Sales Manager. Audit assignments against the current active Sales Manager user list at release and after every membership change. Remove assignments when a user leaves the profile; add one when an active user joins. Manual review does not enforce the rule during the interval between a profile change and assignment update. Salesforce's documented User Access Policies may grant and remove permission sets on user create or update using profile criteria in supported editions. Verify availability, exact criteria, actions, ordering, and profile-entry and profile-exit behavior in this target org before treating that as a dependable mechanism.
- Audit all other permission sets, permission set groups, and profiles for `Tier__c` edit grants. Remove or avoid grants that would let another profile's user edit. Salesforce permissions add together; a read-only profile setting does not cancel another edit grant.
- Field edit access does not replace Account object edit permission or record-level access. Use test Accounts that the Sales Manager and System Administrator users can edit. Verify real profile names and user assignments. Enumerate and test every distinct effective profile, permission-set, and permission-set-group combination among Account viewers, including users with multiple grants.

**Integrations**

- No integration or automation is requested. API clients can read the field only if their Salesforce user has Account and field read access. An update needs Account and field edit access plus record access.

**Operations**

- Deploy the field, permission set, and approved view metadata through the work-item package to the sandbox. Configure profile field permissions in Setup after the field exists. Assign `Account_Tier_Edit` to active Sales Manager users and test a dependable profile-tied assignment process. Record profiles, assignments, the effective-access matrix, and manual release steps for the owner. Agents do not deploy to or change production.
- Review assignments whenever users join or leave the Sales Manager profile. Recheck baseline read and unwanted edit grants when a profile or permission set changes Account access. This option has ongoing assignment work.

| Tradeoff or risk | Effect and response |
| --- | --- |
| Manual `Account_Tier_Edit` assignments do not follow profile membership at the moment it changes. | A missed addition blocks an approved user; a missed removal leaves an unwanted edit grant. Option B is conditional and not recommended on manual assignments alone. Verify a supported, configured User Access Policy or another dependable mechanism in the target org and test both profile entry and exit before selecting it. |
| Profile baseline read and System Administrator edit settings are manual and absent from source control. | Record Setup steps and verify them in each target org. The metadata package alone does not complete access configuration. |

5. Validate and deploy the narrow package to the sandbox using its alias from `.toolkit.json`. Depends on step 4. Complete when Salesforce accepts the metadata and the field appears on the intended layout. Do not target production.
6. Configure baseline field read on every Account-viewing profile and field edit on the System Administrator profile in sandbox Setup. Keep edit off other profiles. Assign `Account_Tier_Edit` only to active Sales Manager profile users. Audit all edit grants. If User Access Policies are available, configure profile-based grant and removal actions for the permission set and verify their action order and triggers; otherwise mark Option B unable to guarantee R-01 and do not recommend it. Depends on step 5. Complete only when assignments and effective grants match the approved rule and the target-org mechanism is verified.
7. Test saving Gold, Silver, Bronze, and blank as Sales Manager and System Administrator users. Test profile entry and exit and confirm the permission-set grant and removal take effect as needed. Check Tier below Rating in every actual assigned Account view. Depends on step 6. # Salesforce component tracker

Keep the deployment records current in the same response as the change.

A project that already uses `engagement/` uses `engagement/deployment/` wherever this skill says `delivery/deployment/`. Do not create a parallel `delivery/` tree. A project with another artifact root keeps these records where it stores deployment records.

## Deployment folder

```
delivery/deployment/
  component-tracker.csv                  one tracker for the whole project
  full-project-deployment-template/
      package.xml                        project-wide manifest; mirrors the tracker
      manual-steps.md                    manual steps for a full project cutover, if needed
  <work-item-id>-<short-name>/  one folder per work item that ships metadata
      DEPLOYMENT-RECORD.md     deployment scope, evidence, and outcome
      package.xml              that item's new and changed components
      destructiveChanges.xml   only if the item removes components
      manual-steps.md          only if the item has manual steps
  <YYYY-MM-DD>-<release-name>/ cutover plan and release notes when needed
```

- One master tracker for the whole project. Never split it per work item.
- `delivery/deployment/full-project-deployment-template/` holds the project-wide manifest and any full-cutover manual steps. Project Init must fill the verified API version before use.
- Name each work-item folder with the work item's id and a short slug from the project's tracker, for example `WI-12-account-merge`. With local tracking, that item is under root `.work-items/`.
- Keep work-item folders flat under `delivery/deployment/`. The tracker owns status.
- A manifest (`package.xml`) names the components a Salesforce CLI deploy includes.

## Step 1: update the tracker, master manifest, and work-item manifest

Do all three in the same response when any of these happens:

1. You author, modify, or rename metadata under `force-app/`.
   - Add the row if none exists, with the correct flags and Change Type. Otherwise edit the existing row.
   - A change to an existing component edits its one row. Never create a second row.
   - Add the member under the correct `<types>` block in `delivery/deployment/full-project-deployment-template/package.xml`. Refresh any member counts in its header when that header uses counts.
   - Add the member to the work item's `package.xml`.
2. The owner reports a successful deploy: set that org's flag to `Yes` for every component in the deploy.
3. You stage a component for deletion:
   - Set Change Type to `Destructive`.
   - Add it to the work item's `destructiveChanges.xml`.
   - Leave the flags showing where it is still present.
4. The owner reports a successful destructive deploy:
   - Set the affected org's flag to `No`.
   - If the component is gone from every org and from `force-app/`, delete the row and its master-manifest member.

Rules for the master manifest:
- Every CLI-deployable tracker row is a member of `delivery/deployment/full-project-deployment-template/package.xml`. Every member has a tracker row.
- A tracker row missing from the master manifest is dropped from the full-org cutover without warning.
- The master manifest is add-only. It never names a removed component.
- These rules apply to every agent and every session.

## Step 2: per-work-item manifests

- `package.xml` names only the work item's new and changed components. Its members also appear in the master manifest.
- Deploy this narrow set, not the master manifest, unless the goal is a full cutover.
- Removals go in `destructiveChanges.xml`, never in a `package.xml`.

## Step 3: types kept out of the manifest

These types cannot be deployed safely by a CLI manifest today: profiles, duplicate rules, matching rules, and compact-layout assignments. They move by change set or by hand.

- Add a tracker row for them. The tracker is the full inventory.
- Keep them out of the master manifest.
- Add their deploy as a step in the relevant `manual-steps.md`: which change set to build, which assignment to make, in what order.
- Name the exclusions in the master manifest's header comment.

Permission sets are not on this list. They get a normal tracker row and a normal manifest member. They deploy by CLI to a sandbox behind the preflight in `permissions-source-control.md`, which also decides when their flag flips.

## Step 4: manual steps (`manual-steps.md`)

Manual deploy steps live in `manual-steps.md` beside the manifest they belong to: the work item's deployment folder, or `delivery/deployment/full-project-deployment-template/` for the full cutover. A folder whose deploy needs no manual steps has no sheet.

Add a step in the same response in which you author the triggering metadata. Triggers:

- New permission set or permission set group: assign it to users.
- New field fed by an external connector: configure the connector mapping.
- New record type that needs retroactive assignment: the data update or Apex script.
- New or changed rollup: capture a pre-deploy baseline and validate the post-deploy delta.
- New scheduled Apex or scheduled flow: schedule it after the deploy.
- Migration that must clear a field before re-stamping: ordered Pre-deploy steps.
- Deploy that depends on a managed-package version, remote site setting, custom setting, or org-wide setting: a Pre-deploy verification step.
- One-time post-deploy backfill (Batch Apex, anonymous Apex, data load): a step with the full kickoff script inline.
- Any deploy where you want a pre-flight snapshot for safe rollback.

Skip the step when the deploy is self-contained:

- Pure UI or LWC changes with no permission, data, or config follow-up.
- Apex refactors that change only internal behavior.
- Formula-field changes that affect only existing in-scope data.
- Label or text-only changes.

When unsure, add the step. A step closed as "skipped" costs less than a missed action.

Step shape:

| Field | Content |
| --- | --- |
| Title | Short imperative step name. |
| Phase | `Pre-deploy`, `Deploy`, or `Post-deploy`. |
| Order | Sequence in the sheet. Use gaps of 10 (10, 20, 30). |
| Owner | Who runs the step. |
| Status | Not started, in progress, or done. |
| Body | Purpose (one or two sentences), numbered operator instructions, a verification section (SOQL, screenshot, or UI check), and inline scripts in fenced code blocks. |

- Put scripts (anonymous Apex, SOQL, CLI commands) inline in the body. Do not link to a repo file for a script that fits inline.
- Link the originating implementation task and any local work-item folder.
- The owner runs the deploys and updates each step's status.

Not in `manual-steps.md`:
- Routine steps that need no ordering.
- Work-item documentation. It lives with the work item.
- Implementation tasks. They live in the task list.
- Generic deploy commands for every Salesforce deploy.

## Tracker schema

Columns, in this fixed order:

| Column | Content |
| --- | --- |
| Component Type | Metadata type: `CustomField`, `CustomObject`, `Flow`, `ApexClass`, `ApexTrigger`, `LightningComponentBundle`, `Layout`, `FlexiPage`, `RecordType`, `QuickAction`, `PermissionSet`, `ValidationRule`, and so on. One value per row. |
| Object/Parent | Parent object for fields, layouts, record types, quick actions, validation rules. Blank for objectless types (Flow, ApexClass, LWC, PermissionSet, CustomApplication, CustomTab). |
| API Name | Full API name including any suffix. |
| Label | Label shown in Setup, or the bundle masterLabel for LWC or Aura. |
| Work Item | One link to the primary task in the project's tracker. Fall back to the work-item folder path. |
| Change Type | `New`, `Modified`, or `Destructive`. |
| Sandbox | `Yes` if deployed in the working sandbox, else `No`. Rename or add columns to match the project's orgs. |
| Production | `Yes` if deployed in production, else `No`. |
| Notes | One short current-state line: type details (`Text(255)`, `Number(18,0)`), what the component does, and any caveat (renamed-from, superseded-by, manual-step, gated-off). Use `;` instead of `,`, or quote the cell. |

## Org flags

- Flags are independent. A component can be in one org, another, or both.
- A new component not yet deployed: all flags `No`.
- When a deploy to an org lands, set that org's flag to `Yes`.
- The owner runs production deploys. When the owner reports a successful production deploy, set `Production=Yes` for its components.
- Order does not matter. `Sandbox=No, Production=Yes` is valid if that is what happened.
- Never change a flag for a failed deploy.

## Change Type

- `New`: this project created the component. Default. A created component that was later renamed is still `New`.
- `Modified`: the component existed and this project changed it. Start Notes with `Modified: ...`.
- `Destructive`: the component is being removed. Keep the row while the deletion is pending in any org. The flags mean "still present there". Delete the row once it is gone from every org and from `force-app/`.

## One row per component

- Key: Component Type + Object/Parent + API Name. One row per key.
- Renamed: keep one row under the new API name, drop the old row, note the rename in Notes.
- Replaced: keep the replacement's row and drop the replaced row, with a note. If the replaced component is still being removed, set its Change Type to `Destructive` until the deletion lands.
- Do not keep rows for components that are gone from `force-app/` and deployed nowhere. The tracker is current state. Git and the task tracker hold history.

## Project-authored only

- Track only components this project created or modified.
- Do not add components pulled into `force-app/` by a backfill or reverse-engineering snapshot. A manifest may list them; the tracker does not.
- A pre-existing component this project modified gets a row with a `Modified: ...` Notes line.

## CSV editing

- Use RFC 4180 quoting. Quote any cell with a comma, newline, or double quote. Escape `"` as `""`.
- Prefer `;` or `/` over `,` inside Notes.
- The header and column order are fixed. Ask the owner before adding a column.
- Group rows by Component Type.

## Not in the tracker

- Config changes made in the org UI with no `force-app/` file.
- Managed-package metadata this project did not author.
- Local-only files: documents, scripts, work-item folders, manifests.
- Dated deploy history. Dates live in the work log or task tracker.

## Related rules

- `check-deployment-contents.md`: reads this tracker as a hint before any deploy.
- `salesforce-org-safety.md`: what an agent may do against an org.
- `permissions-source-control.md`: how permission sets are fetched, verified, and deployed.

  command rule against the plain command. This holds for read commands too:
  `toolkit work decisions && toolkit work show WI-001` is two commands.
- In Codex, a `toolkit` command joined to anything else (`&&`, `;`, a pipe, a
  heredoc, `cd ... &&`) or run from a script (for example Python's
  `subprocess`) runs inside the Codex sandbox. The sandbox blocks Notion,
  Hindsight, and the main checkout's `.work-items/` and `.memory/` from a
  worktree, so the command fails or reports the wrong cause. Run each one
  alone, as its own command.
- Add `--json` when you need to read the output field by field.
- Exit codes: `0` done; `1` error; `2` validation failure (fix what it names
  and run it again); `3` not supported for this tracker or memory backend
  (follow [trackers.md](trackers.md)); `4` not a Toolkit V2 project (open
  `project-setup`).
- "saved but not verified" in the output means the write happened and the
  read-back failed. The message names the first line that differs. Lead the
  reply to the owner with "Saved but not verified", say which line, and read
  the item back to judge it.

## Changing a work item

- Change a work item only through `toolkit work` commands. This keeps the
  local tracker and Notion the same, and it keeps the CLI's record of what it
  wrote. A value the agent changes by hand looks like an owner edit to the
  CLI.
- Find a file only with the command below. Never build a path by hand: the
  owner may have moved or renamed the folder.

  ```text
  toolkit work show <id> --path
  ```

- To change one section of the body, read it, change only what needs to
  change, and write the whole section back. The file holds the same text the
  read printed for that heading, with your changes.

  ```text
  toolkit work show <id> --section "<heading>"
  toolkit work edit <id> --section "<heading>" --set-file <file>
  ```

- To add one row to a table section (Open Questions, Recent History), use
  `--append-row` with the full Markdown table row. A new question takes the
  next free `Q-` number: read the Open Questions section first and add one to
  the highest number there (`Q-01` when there is none).

  ```text
  toolkit work edit <id> --section "Open Questions" --append-row "| <next Q-id> | <question> | R-02 | Open | owner |"
  ```

- Frontmatter values change only through `toolkit work set`, `approve`,
  `design`, `move`, `finish`, and `cancel`. Never edit frontmatter by hand.
- A title is the owner's call. A new item's title uses the owner's own words
  for the request. When you shorten them or choose another, say the title in
  one line in the reply ("I started WI-003, 'Write a short project brief'.").
  To retitle an item, say the new title to him in one line before
  `toolkit work set <id> --title`, and never retitle an item quietly.
- Never hand-edit `.work-items/DASHBOARD.md` or
  `.work-items/.toolkit-state.json`. The hooks refuse it.
- Text for a section or a design:
  - Short or medium text, in both hosts: give it in the command with
    `--text "<text>"`. No file is needed, and newlines inside the quotes are
    kept:

    ```text
    toolkit work edit <id> --section "<heading>" --text "<text>"
    toolkit work design <id> --text "<text>" --status proposed
    ```

  - Claude Code, for long text: pass it on standard input, so no file is left
    anywhere: `toolkit work edit <id> --section "<heading>" --set-file - <<'EOF'`,
    then the text, then `EOF`. (In Codex a heredoc runs the command inside the
    sandbox; use `--text` or a file there.)
  - Codex, for text too long for `--text`: make a new folder for this one save
    with `mktemp -d` (its name is unique, so two sessions or two projects never
    share a file), write the file in it with the file edit tool, run the
    `toolkit` command alone with the file's full path, and delete the file and
    the folder right after the command succeeds (`rm <file>`, then
    `rmdir <folder>`), before you ask the owner anything. Never use a fixed
    name such as `/tmp/wi001-requirements.md`: every project starts at
    `WI-001`, so another session's save could land in this item. Never write
    the file and run the `toolkit` command in one shell command.
  - Never leave draft files inside `.work-items/`: a second `DESIGN.md`-shaped
    file there confuses the design lookup.
- Never write a work item record from the shell (`cat >`, `tee`, `sed -i`,
  `cp`, or a script) and never change its frontmatter with a file edit. The
  hooks refuse both, because they would skip the approval gates.

## Section names in `WORK-ITEM.md`

These are the headings `--section` uses. Every tracker uses the same body: the
project's `.work-items/work-item-template/WORK-ITEM.md`, copied from the model
project.

| Heading | What it holds |
| --- | --- |
| `Overview` | Goal, Current position, Next action (and who owns it), Blockers, Related items (ids, never paths) |
| `Roadmap` | Phases `P1`, `P2` with Outcome, Status, Exit result, Sub-items |
| `Tasks` | Tasks `P1-T01` with Work, Deliverable, Done when, Depends on |
| `Recent History` | Dated rows: change or decision, effect on the work |
| `Open Questions` | `Q-01` rows: question, affects, status, decision needed from (`owner` for the owner) |
| `Requirements` | Overall status, Starting request, Agreed goal, Active requirements `R-01`, Acceptance |
| `Notes` | Decisions and context, Resume here, Solution options and considerations |

The frontmatter fields are `id`, `title`, `type`, `stage`, `status`, `parent`,
`waiting_on`, `priority`, `delivery`, `requirements_approved`, `design`,
`result_approved`, and `updated`. Only `toolkit work` commands change them.

## Section names in `DESIGN.md`

The design has one shape in every tracker (`DESIGN.md` beside a local item,
the "Solution Design" page in Notion, the "Solution design" comment in GitHub
or Jira). The CLI writes its frontmatter: `work_item`, `status` (`proposed`,
`approved`, `superseded`), and `approved`.

| Heading | What it holds |
| --- | --- |
| Header lines | Requirements (the item id), Design status, Requirements checked, Last updated, Design approval |
| `What this design solves` | Who uses the result, what they need, what must be true afterward, and what the design leaves to another item |
| `Requirements and design readiness` | One row per `R-xx`: its status in the item, the design coverage, and the remaining decision or gap |
| `What exists today` | Verified current behavior and files, or "nothing exists yet" |
| `Constraints and assumptions` | One row each, with source, status, and effect on the design |
| `Design options` | `### Option A — <name>` (then B, C) with Approach, End-to-end behavior, Requirement coverage (Build or reuse, Why it meets the requirement, How to check it), Technical shape, Tradeoffs and risks, Build order |
| `Option comparison` | Only with more than one option |
| `Recommendation and owner decision` | Recommendation, Owner decision, Reason for decision |
| `Selected design` | After the owner chooses: End-to-end flow, Components and responsibilities, Data, access, and integration details, Edge cases and failure behavior, Release and ongoing operation |
| `Diagrams` | Mermaid diagrams, each with a heading and a one-sentence explanation |
| `Build and verification plan` | Technical sequence, and Acceptance checks (one row per requirement) |
| `Sources and decisions that affect the build` | Claim or decision, source, date, evidence type, how it was checked |
| `Where a builder could misread this design` | Requirement or section, plausible wrong reading, intended reading |
| `Notes` | Open design questions, Design changes during the interview, Current position and next step |

Keep the headings exactly as the template has them, including the dash in
`Option A — <name>`.

## Saving what the owner says

Save each settled answer in its home before moving to the next topic. An
unanswered question is also information to save. Open decisions do not delay
saving answers that are already settled.

| Information | Home | What to record |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Requirement or correction | The item's `Requirements` section (the `R-xx` block and Acceptance) | The new meaning, and Status `Refining` until approved |
| Design choice | The item's design (`toolkit work design`) | The approach, proposed or approved, and why |
| Open question | The item's `Open Questions` table | Question, what it affects, Open, who must answer (`owner` or a name) |
| Answer or decision about this item | The existing question row, the affected section, and one history note | The answer, who gave it, the date, and whether it is an approval |
| Decision for the whole project | `DECISIONS.md`, through `work-decide` | Decision, why, who decided, what it replaces |
| Outstanding task | The item's `Tasks` section | Work, deliverable, done when, depends on |
| Useful context that is not a requirement | `Notes` > `Decisions and context` | Only what the next session needs |
| Build idea kept for later | `Notes` > `Solution options and considerations` | The idea and the `R-xx` it relates to; it is not a requirement |
| A lasting fact, preference, or lesson | Project memory, through `memory-save` | One record |

- Check the item and memory before asking the owner a question again.
- When sources disagree, keep the conflict open and ask. Do not pick the
  convenient answer.
- A question, a suggestion, a tentative answer, or a saved draft is not
  approval. `toolkit work lifecycle` prints what counts as approval.
- Read the section back after saving. A command that exits `0` is not proof
  by itself.

## Reporting a failed save

- A write failed: lead with "Not saved", name what was not saved and where it
  should go, and keep the text so it can be saved later.
- The write worked and the read-back failed: lead with "Saved but not
  verified".
- Never say "updated" first and correct it later in the same reply.

## When to add a history note

Add one `toolkit work history <id> --note "<text>" --effect "<what it changes>"`
when (without `--effect`, the row says which skill continues the item):

- the stage, type, priority, `waiting_on`, blockers, or next action changes
  for a reason that is not obvious;
- the owner gives a choice, an answer, a requirement, a constraint, an
  approval, or a rejection (quote his words);
- someone outside reports an approval (record who, and do not claim you
  checked it);
- a discovery changes the plan;
- a requested result is finished.

Record the owner's meaning briefly. Do not add reasons, scope, or certainty he
did not give. Do not log routine commands, files opened, ordinary test runs,
or small edits.

## Waiting on the owner

- Set `waiting_on` to `owner` when you ask the owner for an approval or add an
  Open Questions row that he must answer.
- `toolkit work approve` sets `waiting_on` from `owner` to `none`, because the
  owner just answered. After the approval, set it to `agent` when the agent
  continues. After the owner answers his last open question on the item, set
  it back the same way: `agent` when the agent can continue, `none` when
  nothing waits. Keep `owner` only while another question for him on that
  item is still open.

  ```text
  toolkit work set <id> --waiting-on agent
  ```

- An item left at `owner` stays in the briefing and in
  `toolkit work decisions`, and `work-on` sends it to `work-decide` instead of
  its next stage.

## Stages in plain words

- Show a stage with the item id and the plain label from
  `toolkit work lifecycle`, for example "WI-012 is in testing (stage 09)".
- Never ask the owner which stage an item is in. Work it out from the record.
- Status follows the stage. `waiting_on` shows who the item is waiting for.
  Blocked is not a status.

## Owner edits win

The owner may edit the tracker by hand: move a folder, drag a Notion card,
change a stage. The CLI keeps his value, adds a "Changed by hand" history row,
and reports it. Never undo it. When a hand change skips a gate (a build item
moved past stage 03 without approved requirements, or Done without a recorded
result approval), ask the owner about it as a question.

The session briefing lists these changes under "Changes found in the
tracker", and every `toolkit work` command prints the ones it finds. Tell the
owner each one in one line ("You renamed WI-002's folder to help-option; I'll
use the new path.") before other work. The CLI writes the history rows for a
hand move itself: "Moved by hand", "Folder renamed by hand", or "Parent
changed in Notion by hand" on the item, and "Sub-item ... moved out" or
"moved here" on the parents it left and joined. Add a note only for what the
CLI cannot know, such as the owner's reason.

## Branches and worktrees

- An item's code work happens in its own worktree
  `.claude/worktrees/wi-<number>-<slug>` on the branch
  `claude/wi-<number>-<slug>`, the form the project's
  `shared-repository-work.md` rule uses:
  `git worktree add .claude/worktrees/wi-007-csv-export -b claude/wi-007-csv-export`.
  The briefing ties a worktree to its item by the item id in the branch name.
  With another id prefix, use it in lower case (`acme-007-...`).
- Never commit `.work-items/` or `.memory/`. They are Git-ignored and live in
  the main checkout.
- No AI credit anywhere: not in commits, pull requests, comments, or files.
- Codex: its sandbox keeps `.git/` read-only, so `git add`, `git commit`,
  `git worktree add` and `remove`, `git merge`, `git branch -d`, `git fetch`,
  and `git push` cannot run inside it. The project's
  `.codex/rules/toolkit.rules` makes Codex ask the owner before each one.
  - Run each Git write as its own command and ask for escalated permissions:
    set `sandbox_permissions` to `require_escalated`, with a one-line reason
    that says what the command does ("Create the worktree for WI-002 on its own
    branch."). An approval without escalation still runs the command inside
    the sandbox, where it fails on `.git/index.lock`.
  - Tell the owner in one line what the command does before Codex asks.
  - Codex refused it without asking ("approval required by policy, but
    AskForApproval is set to Never"): this session cannot ask. Stop that
    step, show the owner the exact command, ask him to approve it in an
    interactive session or to run it in a terminal, and set the item waiting
    on the owner. It is not an outside blocker.
  - Never work around it: no nested `git clone` of the project, no copy of
    `.git/`, no building on the default branch instead of the item's branch.
- The project's shared-repository rule runs `git fetch origin` before the
  first edit. When `git remote` prints nothing, the project has no remote:
  skip the fetch.
- A merge that stops on a conflict: resolve it, then commit with a message you
  write (`git commit -m "Merge <branch>: <what it brings>"`), never
  `git commit --no-edit`, which keeps Git's "# Conflicts:" lines in the
  message.

# Salesforce component tracker

Keep the deployment records current in the same response as the change.

A project that already uses `engagement/` uses `engagement/deployment/` wherever this skill says `delivery/deployment/`. Do not create a parallel `delivery/` tree. A project with another artifact root keeps these records where it stores deployment records.

## Deployment folder

```
delivery/deployment/
  component-tracker.csv                  one tracker for the whole project
  full-project-deployment-template/
      package.xml                        project-wide manifest; mirrors the tracker
      manual-steps.md                    manual steps for a full project cutover, if needed
  <work-item-id>-<short-name>/  one folder per work item that ships metadata
      DEPLOYMENT-RECORD.md     deployment scope, evidence, and outcome
      package.xml              that item's new and changed components
      destructiveChanges.xml   only if the item removes components
      manual-steps.md          only if the item has manual steps
  <YYYY-MM-DD>-<release-name>/ cutover plan and release notes when needed
```

- One master tracker for the whole project. Never split it per work item.
- `delivery/deployment/full-project-deployment-template/` holds the project-wide manifest and any full-cutover manual steps. Project Init must fill the verified API version before use.
- Name each work-item folder with the work item's id and a short slug from the project's tracker, for example `WI-12-account-merge`. With local tracking, that item is under root `.work-items/`.
- Keep work-item folders flat under `delivery/deployment/`. The tracker owns status.
- A manifest (`package.xml`) names the components a Salesforce CLI deploy includes.

## Step 1: update the tracker, master manifest, and work-item manifest

Do all three in the same response when any of these happens:

1. You author, modify, or rename metadata under `force-app/`.
   - Add the row if none exists, with the correct flags and Change Type. Otherwise edit the existing row.
   - A change to an existing component edits its one row. Never create a second row.
   - Add the member under the correct `<types>` block in `delivery/deployment/full-project-deployment-template/package.xml`. Refresh any member counts in its header when that header uses counts.
   - Add the member to the work item's `package.xml`.
2. The owner reports a successful deploy: set that org's flag to `Yes` for every component in the deploy.
3. You stage a component for deletion:
   - Set Change Type to `Destructive`.
   - Add it to the work item's `destructiveChanges.xml`.
   - Leave the flags showing where it is still present.
4. The owner reports a successful destructive deploy:
   - Set the affected org's flag to `No`.
   - If the component is gone from every org and from `force-app/`, delete the row and its master-manifest member.

Rules for the master manifest:
- Every CLI-deployable tracker row is a member of `delivery/deployment/full-project-deployment-template/package.xml`. Every member has a tracker row.
- A tracker row missing from the master manifest is dropped from the full-org cutover without warning.
- The master manifest is add-only. It never names a removed component.
- These rules apply to every agent and every session.

## Step 2: per-work-item manifests

- `package.xml` names only the work item's new and changed components. Its members also appear in the master manifest.
- Deploy this narrow set, not the master manifest, unless the goal is a full cutover.
- Removals go in `destructiveChanges.xml`, never in a `package.xml`.

## Step 3: types kept out of the manifest

These types cannot be deployed safely by a CLI manifest today: profiles, duplicate rules, matching rules, and compact-layout assignments. They move by change set or by hand.

- Add a tracker row for them. The tracker is the full inventory.
- Keep them out of the master manifest.
- Add their deploy as a step in the relevant `manual-steps.md`: which change set to build, which assignment to make, in what order.
- Name the exclusions in the master manifest's header comment.

Permission sets are not on this list. They get a normal tracker row and a normal manifest member. They deploy by CLI to a sandbox behind the preflight in `permissions-source-control.md`, which also decides when their flag flips.

## Step 4: manual steps (`manual-steps.md`)

Manual deploy steps live in `manual-steps.md` beside the manifest they belong to: the work item's deployment folder, or `delivery/deployment/full-project-deployment-template/` for the full cutover. A folder whose deploy needs no manual steps has no sheet.

Add a step in the same response in which you author the triggering metadata. Triggers:

- New permission set or permission set group: assign it to users.
- New field fed by an external connector: configure the connector mapping.
- New record type that needs retroactive assignment: the data update or Apex script.
- New or changed rollup: capture a pre-deploy baseline and validate the post-deploy delta.
- New scheduled Apex or scheduled flow: schedule it after the deploy.
- Migration that must clear a field before re-stamping: ordered Pre-deploy steps.
- Deploy that depends on a managed-package version, remote site setting, custom setting, or org-wide setting: a Pre-deploy verification step.
- One-time post-deploy backfill (Batch Apex, anonymous Apex, data load): a step with the full kickoff script inline.
- Any deploy where you want a pre-flight snapshot for safe rollback.

Skip the step when the deploy is self-contained:

- Pure UI or LWC changes with no permission, data, or config follow-up.
- Apex refactors that change only internal behavior.
- Formula-field changes that affect only existing in-scope data.
- Label or text-only changes.

When unsure, add the step. A step closed as "skipped" costs less than a missed action.

Step shape:

| Field | Content |
| --- | --- |
| Title | Short imperative step name. |
| Phase | `Pre-deploy`, `Deploy`, or `Post-deploy`. |
| Order | Sequence in the sheet. Use gaps of 10 (10, 20, 30). |
| Owner | Who runs the step. |
| Status | Not started, in progress, or done. |
| Body | Purpose (one or two sentences), numbered operator instructions, a verification section (SOQL, screenshot, or UI check), and inline scripts in fenced code blocks. |

- Put scripts (anonymous Apex, SOQL, CLI commands) inline in the body. Do not link to a repo file for a script that fits inline.
- Link the originating implementation task and any local work-item folder.
- The owner runs the deploys and updates each step's status.

Not in `manual-steps.md`:
- Routine steps that need no ordering.
- Work-item documentation. It lives with the work item.
- Implementation tasks. They live in the task list.
- Generic deploy commands for every Salesforce deploy.

## Tracker schema

Columns, in this fixed order:

| Column | Content |
| --- | --- |
| Component Type | Metadata type: `CustomField`, `CustomObject`, `Flow`, `ApexClass`, `ApexTrigger`, `LightningComponentBundle`, `Layout`, `FlexiPage`, `RecordType`, `QuickAction`, `PermissionSet`, `ValidationRule`, and so on. One value per row. |
| Object/Parent | Parent object for fields, layouts, record types, quick actions, validation rules. Blank for objectless types (Flow, ApexClass, LWC, PermissionSet, CustomApplication, CustomTab). |
| API Name | Full API name including any suffix. |
| Label | Label shown in Setup, or the bundle masterLabel for LWC or Aura. |
| Work Item | One link to the primary task in the project's tracker. Fall back to the work-item folder path. |
| Change Type | `New`, `Modified`, or `Destructive`. |
| Sandbox | `Yes` if deployed in the working sandbox, else `No`. Rename or add columns to match the project's orgs. |
| Production | `Yes` if deployed in production, else `No`. |
| Notes | One short current-state line: type details (`Text(255)`, `Number(18,0)`), what the component does, and any caveat (renamed-from, superseded-by, manual-step, gated-off). Use `;` instead of `,`, or quote the cell. |

## Org flags

- Flags are independent. A component can be in one org, another, or both.
- A new component not yet deployed: all flags `No`.
- When a deploy to an org lands, set that org's flag to `Yes`.
- The owner runs production deploys. When the owner reports a successful production deploy, set `Production=Yes` for its components.
- Order does not matter. `Sandbox=No, Production=Yes` is valid if that is what happened.
- Never change a flag for a failed deploy.

## Change Type

- `New`: this project created the component. Default. A created component that was later renamed is still `New`.
- `Modified`: the component existed and this project changed it. Start Notes with `Modified: ...`.
- `Destructive`: the component is being removed. Keep the row while the deletion is pending in any org. The flags mean "still present there". Delete the row once it is gone from every org and from `force-app/`.

## One row per component

- Key: Component Type + Object/Parent + API Name. One row per key.
- Renamed: keep one row under the new API name, drop the old row, note the rename in Notes.
- Replaced: keep the replacement's row and drop the replaced row, with a note. If the replaced component is still being removed, set its Change Type to `Destructive` until the deletion lands.
- Do not keep rows for components that are gone from `force-app/` and deployed nowhere. The tracker is current state. Git and the task tracker hold history.

## Project-authored only

- Track only components this project created or modified.
- Do not add components pulled into `force-app/` by a backfill or reverse-engineering snapshot. A manifest may list them; the tracker does not.
- A pre-existing component this project modified gets a row with a `Modified: ...` Notes line.

## CSV editing

- Use RFC 4180 quoting. Quote any cell with a comma, newline, or double quote. Escape `"` as `""`.
- Prefer `;` or `/` over `,` inside Notes.
- The header and column order are fixed. Ask the owner before adding a column.
- Group rows by Component Type.

## Not in the tracker

- Config changes made in the org UI with no `force-app/` file.
- Managed-package metadata this project did not author.
- Local-only files: documents, scripts, work-item folders, manifests.
- Dated deploy history. Dates live in the work log or task tracker.

## Related rules

- `check-deployment-contents.md`: reads this tracker as a hint before any deploy.
- `salesforce-org-safety.md`: what an agent may do against an org.
- `permissions-source-control.md`: how permission sets are fetched, verified, and deployed.

# The dependency edge list: what connects to what in a Salesforce org

This folder reads a Salesforce org's metadata files and writes down every
connection it can find between them: which flow reads which field, which Apex
class writes which object, which permission set grants access to what, which
layout shows which field. The result is a set of JSON files you can query.

It answers two questions:

1. **Where does this value come from?** What writes this field, or what is it
   computed from?
2. **If I rename or change this, what breaks?** Everything that names it, out to
   however many steps you ask for.

**Building the edge list never contacts a Salesforce org.** No network, no `sf`
commands, no authentication. It reads the files under `force-app/` and nothing
else.

Four files here do contact an org, and they are the optional cross-check:
`org_api.py`, `pull_org_dependencies.py`, `org_catalog.py` and
`build_org_catalog.py`. Every call any of them makes is `sf data query`, which is
a read. Nothing in this folder ever writes to an org, deploys, validates, or runs
Apex. Assume the org is production, because it usually is.

Python standard library only. There is nothing to install.

## Where the org names come from

The tool knows an org by the folder its metadata sits in. Nothing is hardcoded,
so the same code runs against one org or ten, whatever they are called.

Two layouts are understood, in this order:

1. **`sfdx-project.json` lists its `packageDirectories`.** Each one is an org,
   named by the last segment of its path, with its metadata at
   `<path>/main/default`. A project pointing at `force-app/red` and
   `force-app/blue` gets orgs called `red` and `blue`. An ordinary single-package
   project pointing at `force-app` gets one org called `force-app`.
2. **No `sfdx-project.json`**, so every folder directly under `force-app` holding
   a `main/default` is an org.

A package directory holding no metadata is skipped rather than reported as an
empty org. Naming an org that has no metadata stops with an error listing the
orgs the project does have, rather than handing back an empty answer that looks
real.

**The Salesforce CLI needs a different name.** The two scripts that contact an
org pass the org name to `sf -o`, and a CLI alias is often not the folder name.
The folder name is used as-is unless the project says otherwise in
`tools/kb/org-aliases.json` beside these files:

```json
{"red": "RED", "blue": "BLUE"}
```

`--alias <org>=<CLI target>` overrides that for one run. A project whose folder
names already match its CLI aliases needs neither.

## Build it first

Nothing the tool writes is committed. The output is rebuilt from `force-app/` on
demand, which takes roughly 25 seconds an org, so there is no stored copy that
can go out of date.

```bash
python tools/kb/build_edges.py                  # every org in the project
python tools/kb/build_edges.py --org <name>     # one named org
```

That one command writes five files per org into `tools/kb/out/`:

| File | What it holds |
| --- | --- |
| `edges-<org>.json` | Every component and every edge, with the file and element each edge came from. |
| `reverse-index-<org>.json` | What points AT each component, so "what depends on X" needs only this file. |
| `coverage-<org>.json` | Every file on disk, its metadata type, how many edges it produced, and when that count is zero, the reason. |
| `unresolved-<org>.json` | Every name that resolved to nothing, with its reason, the rule that decided, and who asked for it. |
| `reports-<org>.md` | The readable version of the last two, about 300 lines. |

Size depends on the org. In the project this was built in, one org's edge list
came to 213.6 MB and another's to 51.6 MB, with the reverse index at 36.3 MB and
8.7 MB. **Do not commit these.** GitHub warns above 50 MB a file and refuses
anything above 100 MB, so add `tools/kb/out/` to `.gitignore` and rebuild
instead.

The four JSON files are written one entry to a line, so an ordinary text search
returns one edge rather than the whole file, and each file is still a single
valid JSON document. There is no timestamp inside any of them: two builds of the
same snapshot are byte-identical, which is what lets two builds be compared.

```bash

python tools/kb/query_graph.py Case.Priority

# The same, reaching three steps out instead of two
python tools/kb/query_graph.py --org <name> "<name>:Flow:Case_Escalation" --hops 3

# A name that points at nothing: who asked for it, and why did it not resolve?
python tools/kb/query_graph.py --org <name> --unresolved npsp__Household__c

# What is in this org, ranked by how connected each thing is?
python tools/kb/query_graph.py --org <name> --map

# How does each field get its value?
python tools/kb/classify_fields.py
python tools/kb/classify_fields.py --org <name> --field Case.Priority

## What this design solves

The sales team needs to rank Accounts with an optional Tier field. Gold, Silver, and Bronze must appear in that order, with Gold highest and no default. Every Account viewer must be able to read Tier. Only Sales Manager profile users and system administrators may edit it. Tier must appear directly below Rating on Account Layout and have a description and help text. This design covers the field, access, layout, and verification. It does not change existing Account data.

# Local project memory

Keep future sessions oriented without turning every conversation into lasting memory. This folder is the project's built-in memory store and can be opened directly as an Obsidian vault. Active topics stay flat; filenames and YAML types agree. Git ignores this folder, so back it up with `toolkit memory export --to <folder outside this project>`.

## Read and route

- Read `CURRENT_FOCUS.md` at startup; the session briefing includes it. Read `MEMORY.md` as a short index, then open relevant topics. Check dates, scope, and the current source before acting on a remembered claim.
- Read `memory-criteria.md` before selecting or changing memory. It holds the default eligibility rules; the `memory-save` skill holds the approval policy and the onboarding or trusted mode. Use the terminology glossary for project language, including distinct meanings across systems.
- Link related notes inside this vault with relative Markdown links, such as `[account model](project_account_model.md)`. Obsidian shows backlinks to a note from the notes that link to it; a second reverse link is optional. Link only when the relationship helps retrieval, and check that the target exists. Keep tracker URLs and paths outside `.memory/` as source references rather than vault links.
- Keep current tasks and owner-mentioned to-dos in `CURRENT_FOCUS.md`, naming work items by ID. Keep full tasks, status, requirements, history, and the work item's design together in the chosen tracker; verified system behavior in the System Guide; procedures in instructions or skills; and raw outside sources in their source folders.

## Curate

- Use a coherent topic file such as `project_account_data_model.md`. Allowed prefixes and matching `metadata.type` values are `user`, `feedback`, `project`, `reference`, and `event`. `project_topic_template.md` is a seed, not a saved memory. Keep one related topic per file and aim for a quick read.
- Record source and date, status, scope, the durable point, why it matters, and how to apply it. Keep uncertainty explicit. Preserve extra YAML fields written by a host or imported record.
- Search for an existing topic before creating one (`toolkit memory find`). Correct, merge, or supersede in place where possible. Mark obsolete claims in both file text and index; do not leave an archived item reading as currently open.
- When renaming, merging, archiving, or deleting a topic, inspect links from other memory notes and repair any affected links, saving each repaired note with `toolkit memory save`. Do not leave a link pointing at a former active location.
- `toolkit memory save`, `retire`, and `restore` rebuild `MEMORY.md`; run `toolkit memory reindex` after any other topic change. The index holds one short link per active topic, not the content itself. Keep it below the configured budget.
- Keep `CURRENT_FOCUS.md` under 50 lines by replacing stale sections, not appending, and write it with `toolkit memory focus --set-file`. Do not remove an unresolved owner to-do solely to meet that limit.
- Keep the glossary broad through sourced real terms, aliases, and system-specific meanings, and write it with `toolkit memory glossary --set-file`. Do not invent definitions.

## Authority and completion

- Save through the `memory-save` skill, which holds the approval policy for onboarding and trusted mode. An explicit request to remember or correct is authorization for that specific change.
- Ask before ambiguous, bulk, or irreversible deletion of unique content. Only the owner can change the mode.
- A rejected candidate is not saved to another memory, a criteria example, the glossary, or a pending queue. Record only the general selection lesson, as a `feedback` memory, if the owner gave one.
- The main agent writes this folder only with `toolkit memory` commands (`save`, `retire`, `restore`, `delete`, `focus`, `glossary`, `reindex`). They lock the folder, refuse stale edits, and rebuild the index. Never run parallel writers against the same topic.
- Read back changes with `toolkit memory get` and run `toolkit doctor` before reporting success. Memory work does not edit requirements, work-item status, designs, deployments, or source code.
# Memory criteria

This file is the project-specific selection policy: what is worth keeping in lasting memory. The approval policy, including onboarding and trusted mode, is in the `memory-save` skill, which saves with `toolkit memory save`. When the owner corrects what is worth saving, save the correction as a `feedback` memory with `memory-save`, as a general rule, without copying the rejected memory. Those `feedback` memories override this page.

## Default test for lasting memory

Save a topic when it concerns this project, has a credible source, would matter in a future session, would be costly or unreliable to reconstruct, and has no better maintained owner. Prefer updating an existing topic. A short pointer to an authoritative record can qualify when future sessions would otherwise miss that record.

| Type and filename | Usually worth retaining | Route or reject instead |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `user_<topic>.md` | Relevant role, responsibility, working preference, or communication need the owner stated | Personal judgments, irrelevant biography, private details |
| `feedback_<topic>.md` | Repeated or standing correction to how the agent should work; confirmed selection lesson | One-off irritation, a rejected fact restated as policy, an instruction already in `AGENTS.md` |
| `project_<topic>.md` | Durable project constraint, rationale, technical landmark, or proven costly fix | A decision for the whole project (`DECISIONS.md`), code summary, schema copy, active ticket status, accepted requirement or design body |
| `reference_<topic>.md` | Hard-to-rediscover route to a source, system, dashboard, or decision record, with why to open it | Entire outside page or a path already obvious in `PROJECT.md` or the project map |
| `event_<topic>.md` | Significant project episode: what was done, what resulted, and where the output lives | Routine edit, tool call, raw error, daily progress log |

## Working context is different

`CURRENT_FOCUS.md` holds what is happening now: active work item IDs, what waits on the owner with no work item, untracked to-dos, and where the next session starts. It can change often. Keep a work item's detailed tasks and status in that item. Do not turn every open task into lasting memory. Do not discard an unresolved owner to-do merely to shorten the file.

## Never save as lasting memory

- Secrets, credentials, sensitive personal data, transcripts, scratch reasoning, raw logs, dropped guesses, or unsupported claims.
- A fact the same change already places in the authoritative file, unless a small route to that file is genuinely needed.
- Live status, pending approval, unshipped requirements, procedure steps, code restatements, or a current-system explanation that the code/System Guide owns.
- A rejected candidate under a new name or wider wording. A rejection stands until the owner changes it.

This folder is Git-ignored. Back it up with `toolkit memory export --to <folder outside this project>` and restore a fresh clone with `toolkit memory import --from <that folder>`. Linked worktrees resolve to one vault in the main checkout. A fresh clone or machine needs its memory restored before the agent treats an empty index as evidence that no memory exists.

In Codex, a `toolkit` command joined to anything else (`&&`, `;`, a pipe, a heredoc) or run from a script runs inside the sandbox, which blocks Hindsight and Notion: run it alone. Text: give it in the command with `--body "<text>"` (a save) or `--text "<text>"` (the focus or the glossary), so no file is needed. For a long text, in Claude Code pass it on standard input (`--set-file -` or `--body-file -` with a heredoc); in Codex make a new folder for each save with `mktemp -d`, write the file there, and delete the file and the folder right after the command succeeds. ## Steps

1. Decide the home first, with the memory criteria (`.memory/memory-criteria.md` with built-in memory; otherwise `references/record-format.md`). Memory holds a lasting preference, correction, fact about the project or the owner, or a hard-to-find reference. Elsewhere: project work goes to `work-on`; a decision for the whole project to `work-decide` (`DECISIONS.md`); delivered behavior to `requirements/`; how a change is built to the item's design; verified current structure to `system-guide/`; outside documentation to `ai-external-knowledge/`; a standing rule for how agents work here is proposed as a rule-file change; an owner to-do with no work item goes to the current focus "Untracked to-dos"; a project term goes to the glossary. A short memory pointer to a hard-to-find record is allowed; never copy its body.
2. Search first and update the existing record rather than add a duplicate.
   `toolkit memory find "<topic>"`
   `toolkit memory get <key>`
3. Approval. This is the only written copy of the memory approval policy. Read the mode, then apply it:
   `toolkit config get memory.approval`

Always ask first, in either mode, for anything about a named person, personal details, a hard delete, more than five records at once, or a change to this policy. A yes covers only the change and meaning shown. Silence is never a yes. There is no proposal inbox: keep an unanswered question in the conversation and go on with other work.
4. Save: type (`user`, `feedback`, `project`, `reference`, `event`), slug, one-line description, the source, and a body file with the model's labels: Remember, Why (the owner's reason in his words, or "Not stated by the owner."; never a reason you inferred), How to apply, Evidence and limits (the source and an absolute date), Related memories (relative links such as `[deploy window](project_deploy_window.md)`), Authoritative records. Giving the same record a better name, or a type that matches its content: rename it; links to it are repaired. Use the first save form when the owner approved (his words or his yes); the second only for a routine save in `trusted` mode.
